content:
Hello, I am a first time contributor. I am a paramedic, and decidedly not a mathematician, however I found that mathlib was missing this, and figured it was something worth trying out.

I have a formalization of Vaughan's identity (1977, the von Mangoldt decomposition), sitting on a public GitHub branch. It is not yet a PR, because I read on the contribution guide, and wanted to make sure I am doing this right. Below is the info for my branch:

Branch: https://github.com/cjfendt/mathlib4/tree/vaughan-identity
File: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ArithmeticFunction/Vaughan.lean (~70 lines incl. docs)
Builds green against current master; lake exe runLinter passes on the module.
Proof reduces to ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_mul_zeta plus ring algebra in the
Dirichlet convolution ring; adds a small trunc (truncation) helper def.

The Lean code was written mainly by Claude Code, at my direction. I simply made it do the work and iterated it against the compiler, as I am not a Lean expert and won't act like I am.

I read the contribution guide, and wanted to make sure I was doing this correctly; if a PR is welcomed, it needs to carry the appropriate flag, as I am a new account, and cannot apply a label, and I want to make sure I am at least alerting those who need to know of where I am coming from.

The math checks out (compiled and delinted), the statement matches the literature as I understand it, and the thing I can't verify is why I come here, to ensure that style fit is done correctly.

Is a PR welcome under the policies as they stand, considering how I went about doing this? I would appreciate if someone is able to review my branch, if so, and am okay if the answer is no, I am just trying to be helpful when bored.

Thanks!
